components.name: Market Momentum
components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The index closed 7,575.39 on Friday 10 July, a fresh weekly high (+>1% on the week) back above a rising 125-day average and within ~1% of its record as tech leadership reasserted (Nvidia +4%, Meta +15% on the week) — momentum has firmed to the constructive side.

components.name: Stock Price Strength
components.reading: Net 52-week highs vs lows on the NYSE. Net new highs stayed positive as the tape recovered from the 7 July chip wobble; breadth broadened again with ~63% of the S&P above its 50-DMA (up from ~50% a month ago), keeping this reading neutral-to-constructive.

components.name: Stock Price Breadth
components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). The Summation Index resumed its climb after the brief 7 July semis rout as participation rebroadened into the 10 July winning week, pushing the short-term McClellan Oscillator back positive.

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Options buyers stayed modestly defensive into the 14 July June CPI print, but the calm tape and equity rally trimmed put demand versus late June — a neutral read rather than fear.

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. The VIX stayed calm in the mid-teens through the 10 July rally — well below its 50-day average despite a firmer 10-year and the Iran-truce noise, a decidedly non-fearful read.

components.name: Safe-Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Equities outpaced Treasuries over the trailing window as the 10-year backed up ~9bp on the week to ~4.57% (highest since 22 May on firmer oil and hawkish-Fed repricing), so stocks-over-bonds performance nudges this toward neutral.

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. HY OAS remains historically tight and IG saw its biggest inflow since June 2020 (+$16.7B, wk to 2 July), keeping demand for credit firm but with a quality tilt — a neutral-to-mildly-greedy read.

metrics.value: ~63% on 10 July, up from ~50% a month ago — a clear sign of broadening short-term participation (Schwab/Barchart $S5FI)

metrics.value: Advancers led on the 10 July up session as the S&P rose 0.42% to 7,575; broad-based buying (a healthier internal than the 7 July semis-led down day)

metrics.value: Net positive and re-widening as the index reclaimed weekly highs; precise live counts not extractable from JS-rendered tables (approximate)

metrics.label: NYSE McClellan Oscillator / Summation Index
metrics.value: Summation Index trending higher on rebroadening breadth; the short-term Oscillator swung back positive after the 7 July tech rout (mcoscillator.com; exact daily NYMO not published in accessible sources; approximate)

metrics.value: Rising and near highs — the broad A-D line continues to confirm the tape, a healthier picture than the narrow mega-cap-only leadership of earlier in 2026 (approximate trend read)

metrics.value: ~73-82% (roughly 8-9 of 11 sector ETFs) as leadership stayed broad across Financials, Industrials, Health Care and Tech; consistent with the ~65% S5TH reading (inferred)

breadth.note: Breadth stayed broad and constructive into 10 July: ~63% of the S&P sits above its 50-DMA (up from ~50% a month ago) and roughly two-thirds above the 200-DMA, with the cumulative A-D line near highs and 8-9 of 11 sectors above trend. The 7 July semiconductor wobble was fully recovered as tech re-led a winning week (Nvidia +4%, Meta +15%). The open question is whether the 14 July June CPI print lets the broadening continue or re-narrows the tape around a hawkish, higher-for-longer Warsh Fed.

flows.period: Week ending 2 July 2026 (BofA 'Flow Show' citing EPFR Global). Flows are weekly and lagged; a newer week may exist but is not yet itemized in free sources.
flows.narrative: The rotation out of crowded US mega-cap growth into cash, duration and credit deepened. In the week to 2 July, money-market funds pulled in a huge +$56.4B and bonds +$20.5B — led by investment-grade credit's biggest inflow since June 2020 (+$16.7B) — while US growth funds bled -$5.0B (worst since March) and US mid-caps -$5.7B (worst since July 2023). Headline equity funds still netted +$2.2B, but US equities saw a second straight weekly outflow (-$1.9B) and Japan a fourth (-$2.8B); only Europe kept drawing money (+$0.6B, third straight week). Gold (+$1.4B) and crypto (+$1B) both stayed positive. Notably, Treasuries broke their long inflow streak with a -$2.7B outflow (largest in 9 weeks) as the 10-year backed up toward 4.57% — money favored spread product over duration.

regions.note: Second consecutive weekly outflow. The pain was concentrated in style: US growth -$5.0B (worst since March) and US mid-cap -$5.7B (worst since July 2023), even as the headline all-equity number stayed positive at +$2.2B.
Third straight week of European-equity inflows — the pro-international tilt of 2026 persists as investors trim US concentration.
EM equity funds resumed outflows after a firmer June; flows choppy as China caps its rally and the dollar stays firm.

Mainland-China equity funds still leaking as authorities manage the pace of the rally; offshore HK tech ripped on 8 July (HSTECH +5%, Alibaba +12%) but that is price, not fund-flow. China bond funds remain on an inflow streak. Specific weekly figure not public — approximate.
Fourth consecutive week of Japanese-equity outflows as the yen sat near 40-year lows and investors rotated away from the crowded Japan trade.

A large surge back into cash — the opposite of the prior week's redemption — as hawkish-Fed repricing and a firmer 10-year made ~3.6-3.75% parked yield attractive and risk appetite for crowded US growth cooled.

Investment-grade credit drew +$16.7B — its biggest inflow since June 2020 — but Treasuries broke their long streak with a -$2.7B outflow (largest in 9 weeks) as duration was shunned into the CPI print. The bid is for spread/carry, not rates.
Gold funds stayed positive (+$1.4B) even as spot slipped toward $4,050-4,075 — a steady central-bank-and-hedge bid under the price despite the firm dollar.

movements.note: The marquee rotation of the week — the biggest US-growth outflow since March and the biggest mid-cap outflow since July 2023, with the proceeds parked in money funds ahead of the 14 July CPI.

Duration was shunned (largest UST outflow in 9 weeks) while IG credit saw its biggest inflow since June 2020 — investors want carry and spread, not rate risk, with the 10-year backing up toward 4.57%.
The pro-international, anti-US-concentration tilt persisted (Europe's third straight inflow week) alongside a steady gold and crypto (+$1B) bid.
